decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Search”; round 1 client: “search ... feel[s] like what I wanted.”
decisions.note: Prototype review. The presentation does not identify which bookmark fields are searched, so conformity with the full-text-search requirement cannot be established; the client’s approval does not resolve that uncertainty.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “collections”; round 1 client: “the collections ... feel like what I wanted.”
decisions.note: Prototype review. It is unclear whether collections are functionally equivalent to multi-valued tags and tag filtering. Bare approval does not establish those semantics.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “unread filters”; round 1 client positively identifies the “unread filter.”
decisions.note: Prototype review. A separate unread filter conforms to the requirement to view only unread bookmarks.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Grid and list layouts” and “Polished editorial visual system”; round 1 client: “the layout ... feel[s] like what I wanted.”
decisions.note: Prototype review. A list is presented, but the transcript does not establish whether each item exposes the required title, description, tags, and favicon. General praise does not resolve this.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents an “Add ... workflow”; round 1 client reports, “it made me type in the title and the description myself,” rejects that burden, and says, “I just paste the link.” Round 2 maker confirms this was changed by stating, “Implemented the quick-save flow.”
decisions.note: Prototype review. Requiring manual title and description entry contradicts URL-only quick saving, and the client explicitly rejects that behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client identifies the observed omission: “it made me type in the title and the description myself,” then supplies the expected behavior: “saving a link pulls in the page’s title and description on its own” plus “its little icon.” Round 2 maker: “Implemented the quick-save flow.”
decisions.note: Prototype review. The initial add flow lacked automatic metadata collection; the client supplied the reference-conforming behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “edit ... workflows”; round 1 client: “the edit/delete controls all feel like what I wanted.”
decisions.note: Prototype review. The transcript does not establish whether URL, title, description, tags, and note are all editable. The client’s general approval is not a clarifying disposition.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “delete workflows”; round 1 client says the “edit/delete controls ... feel like what I wanted.”
decisions.note: Prototype review. The presented delete workflow conforms to bookmark deletion.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Favorite and read-status controls”; round 1 client positively identifies the unread functionality.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Read-status controls conform to marking bookmarks unread/read; no contrary behavior is presented.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “when you paste a link” metadata is fetched; round 2 client confirms, “I pasted a link and it pulled in the page’s name and description on its own.”
decisions.note: Implementation review. The revised quick-save flow conforms to saving through URL entry.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker enumerates automatic retrieval of “title, description, and favicon” but not the required preview image. Round 2 client repeats only the page name and description and concludes, “I’m happy with it.”
decisions.note: Implementation review. The revised metadata decision still omits preview-image collection. The client does not identify that difference; final approval alone is not an accepted divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “Retrieved fields remain editable”; round 2 client confirms, “I could still adjust them before saving,” alongside the previously presented edit workflow.
decisions.note: Implementation review. Editable fetched fields before saving, together with the existing edit workflow, conforms to editing collected title/description before and after saving.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “Sites that block metadata fetching can still be saved manually.” Round 2 client accepts the completed flow without discussing this fallback.
decisions.note: Implementation review. A manual fallback after an attempted fetch does not contradict automatic collection in the normal case and preserves the ability to save a URL.
